description:
Design a Verilog module that implements a simple state machine for an SD card interface. The state machine should have the following states: IDLE, READ, WRITE, and ERROR. The module should have a clock input, a reset input, and a start signal. The state transitions should be as follows: 
- From IDLE to READ on start signal
- From IDLE to WRITE on start signal
- From READ to IDLE on read complete signal
- From WRITE to IDLE on write complete signal
- Any state can transition to ERROR on error signal
The module should output the current state of the state machine.
code:
module sd_card_fsm (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire start,
    input wire read_complete,
    input wire write_complete,
    input wire error,
    output reg [1:0] state // 00: IDLE, 01: READ, 10: WRITE, 11: ERROR
);

    parameter IDLE = 2'b00, READ = 2'b01, WRITE = 2'b10, ERROR = 2'b11;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= IDLE;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                IDLE: begin
                    if (start) begin
                        state <= (start && !read_complete) ? READ : WRITE;
                    end
                end
                READ: begin
                    if (read_complete) begin
                        state <= IDLE;
                    end else if (error) begin
                        state <= ERROR;
                    end
                end
                WRITE: begin
                    if (write_complete) begin
                        state <= IDLE;
                    end else if (error) begin
                        state <= ERROR;
                    end
                end
                ERROR: begin
                    if (reset) begin
                        state <= IDLE;
                    end
                end
                default: state <= IDLE;
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

module adaptive_lms_filter (
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input signed [15:0] x,      // Input signal
    input signed [15:0] d,      // Desired signal
    output reg signed [15:0] y   // Output signal
);
    parameter N = 5;            // Number of taps
    parameter mu = 16'sd1;      // Step size
    reg signed [15:0] w [0:N-1]; // Coefficients
    reg signed [15:0] x_buf [0:N-1]; // Input buffer
    integer i;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            for (i = 0; i < N; i = i + 1) begin
                w[i] <= 16'sd0; // Initialize weights
                x_buf[i] <= 16'sd0; // Initialize buffer
            end
            y <= 16'sd0; // Initialize output
        end else begin
            // Shift input buffer
            for (i = N-1; i > 0; i = i - 1) begin
                x_buf[i] <= x_buf[i-1];
            end
            x_buf[0] <= x; // New input

            // Calculate output
            y <= 16'sd0;
            for (i = 0; i < N; i = i + 1) begin
                y <= y + (w[i] * x_buf[i]); // Filter output
            end

            // Update weights
            for (i = 0; i < N; i = i + 1) begin
                w[i] <= w[i] + (mu * (d - y) * x_buf[i]); // LMS update
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

module kalman_filter (
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input [15:0] sensor1,
    input [15:0] sensor2,
    output reg [15:0] estimated_value
);

    reg [15:0] p;     // Estimate covariance
    reg [15:0] q;     // Process noise covariance
    reg [15:0] r;     // Measurement noise covariance
    reg [15:0] k;     // Kalman Gain

        x = 16'h0000;  // Initial state estimate
        p = 16'hFFFF;  // Initial covariance
        q = 16'h0001;  // Process noise
        r = 16'h0002;  // Measurement noise
    end

        if (rst) begin
            x <= 16'h0000;
            p <= 16'hFFFF;
        end else begin

            // Measurement Update Step
            k <= p / (p + r);
            x <= x + k * (sensor1 + sensor2)/2 - x; // Average of sensor1 and sensor2
            p <= (16'hFFFF - k) * p; // Update covariance

            estimated_value <= x; // Output the estimated value
        end
    end
